title: What If You Had a Dog's Sense of Smell?

scenes.text: What if you had a dog's sense of smell? Walking into a bakery would never be the same.
A dog has up to 300 million scent receptors. You have about six million.
The part of its brain that analyzes smell is proportionally about 40 times bigger than ours.
Scientists estimate its nose is 10,000 to 100,000 times as sensitive, enough to detect a teaspoon of sugar in two Olympic pools.
Dogs even keep scent flowing in a separate path. When we exhale, we lose the smell.
In that bakery, a dog could pick out apples, butter, cinnamon and nutmeg. You would just smell pie.
